priorities.suggestion: Use `WHERE ... IN (?)` to batch 10 queries into one

suggested_fix.recommendation: Rewrite the per-id loop as a single query with a `JOIN` or `WHERE id IN (...)`. With `JdbcTemplate`, bind the id list through `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate`, or on PostgreSQL pass one array via `= ANY(?)`.

priorities.plain: The application sends one small message per item instead of grouping them into one.
priorities.suggestion: Send 6 messages as one batch instead of one publish per item

suggested_fix.recommendation: Let the producer batch: publish the records without calling `flush()` or blocking on each `send()` future, and tune `linger.ms` / `batch.size` so records to the same partition coalesce into one broker request.

priorities.plain: For each item, the application asks another part of the system again, instead of asking once for the whole list.
priorities.suggestion: Use a batch endpoint with `?ids=...` to batch 5 calls into one

suggested_fix.recommendation: Coalesce the calls into a batch endpoint, or cache the per-request results with `Spring`'s `@Cacheable` using a request-scoped cache.

priorities.plain: The application asks another part of the system the same question several times for one action, when once would do.
priorities.suggestion: Identical operation executed 3 times: cache result or deduplicate

suggested_fix.recommendation: Wrap the HTTP client in a request-scoped memoization layer (`Caffeine`, a `HashMap` on a request-scoped bean, or `Spring`'s `@Cacheable` with a request-scoped key) so identical calls return the cached response within the request.

priorities.plain: The application fetches the same information several times for one action, when once would do.
priorities.suggestion: Identical operation executed 3 times: cache result or deduplicate

suggested_fix.recommendation: Add a service-level cache (`Caffeine`, `Spring Cache`) or deduplicate the query within the request scope.

priorities.plain: Two parts of the system exchange many small messages for one action, where a few larger ones would do.
priorities.suggestion: Chatty trace: GET /api/dashboard/home triggers 16 inter-service HTTP calls (top: GET achievement-svc/api/achievements/recent x1, GET activity-svc/api/activity/feed x1). Consider aggregating calls with a batch endpoint or a BFF (Backend for Frontend) layer

priorities.plain: A single action sets a large number of other parts of the system to work at once.
priorities.suggestion: Parent span has 21 children (threshold: 20). Consider batching child operations to reduce fanout.

priorities.plain: Actions wait in line because the application can only reach its data a few at a time.
priorities.suggestion: Potential connection pool saturation: service orders-svc has 10 concurrent SQL spans within 0ms window. Consider increasing the connection pool size, optimizing long-running queries or using connection pool metrics (db.client.connection.pool.*) for precise monitoring

priorities.plain: Waiting on another part of the system takes long enough to make people wait.
priorities.suggestion: Consider caching or optimizing endpoint

suggested_fix.recommendation: Profile the upstream's own `slow_sql` / `slow_http` findings first (the latency is usually upstream-side). On the client, wrap the call in a `Resilience4j` circuit breaker with a tight timeout, and cache the response when staleness tolerance allows.

priorities.plain: Fetching some information takes long enough to make people wait.
priorities.suggestion: Consider adding an index or optimizing query

suggested_fix.recommendation: Profile with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`. Add an index on the columns used in `WHERE` + `ORDER BY` when selectivity justifies it. If the plan is dominated by a nested loop on a large outer, rewrite to push the selective predicate first.

priorities.plain: The application does several steps one after another that could run at the same time, so people wait longer than needed.

How to read this report

The period
A week runs Monday to Sunday and a month is a calendar month, both counted in UTC days. While the period is in progress, trends compare its closed days with the same days of the previous period; today counts in the tiles only. Times elsewhere on the page are in your local time, with the zone.
Avoidable I/O
Extra database, HTTP and messaging calls the engine counted as avoidable on this period, summed over the detections. Measured, not estimated.
CO2 estimate
An order of magnitude, never a ranking key: each finding's avoidable calls times the day's grams per avoidable call the daemon reports. "At least" when some sources send no coefficient.
Active findings
Findings seen on this period and not acknowledged. Acknowledged ones are counted apart and left out of the priorities.
Actions
Declared by the team, checked by the engine: confirmed after a sealed day with no detection, still detected when it shows up after the done day.
What to fix first
Findings with avoidable calls first, by volume; then the others by severity. Trends compare closed days only.
What moved
Gone means not detected this period: a presumption, not proof that the fix shipped.
